recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-7750 unless the Security work group separately reopens the broader Provenance lifecycle/action questions.
issue_request: FHIR-7750 was a Published FHIR-core Security change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking to rationalize Provenance and decouple it from AuditEvent. The accepted resolution narrowed the work to updating the AuditEvent introduction to explain that all actors involved in an auditable event should record an AuditEvent and that duplicate AuditEvent records are expected in a system of systems.
initial_application: No relevant source commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-7750 was found. Git history shows the apparent implementation in 26bc7b5249d06a0d7214f1523bb52b2b1a1d8d20, which updated the AuditEvent and Provenance introductions after the Security WG vote and added the all-actors/duplicate-records AuditEvent guidance.
additional_context: AuditEvent and Provenance are active resources in source/fhir.ini. FHIR-7567 was cited from FHIR-7750 comments and resolved related Provenance/W3C alignment concerns through other CPs. Later issues FHIR-9407 and FHIR-9417 support keeping AuditEvent.action, Provenance.activity, and lifecycle concepts distinct rather than adding new coupling. Community searches found no conflicting Zulip or Confluence evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current source/auditevent/auditevent-introduction.xml already says all actors involved in an auditable event SHOULD record an AuditEvent and explains why duplicate entries are expected and useful for detecting problems.
